title: Ephemeral reserve orchestration for weights / KV / activations (dynamic rebalancer)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Current static partitioning between model weights, KV cache, and activations forces conservative per-GPU headroom settings to avoid OOMs under bursty mixed workloads. That overprovisioning increases cost and reduces throughput for steady-state workloads. Existing approaches (static ledgers, fixed headroom percentage) don't adapt well to workload shifts (long context chat + short completion spikes).

Proposal:
Introduce an Ephemeral Reserve Orchestration (ERO) component inside the serving runtime that: (1) maintains a small, dynamically-sized ephemeral reserve pool per GPU that can be lent to KV/activations temporarily; (2) runs a continuous rebalancer loop that observes allocation pressure signals (KV hit-miss ratio, active batch size distribution, allocation failures, activation growth rate) and redistributes the reserve between weight-safe region and active allocations; (3) uses a cost-based eviction heuristic to choose whether to evict KV entries, compress/quantize activations in-place or reject/buffer new requests; (4) exposes a soft-lease API (soft-lease tokens) to front-end schedulers to signal available ephemeral capacity for larger batches.

Key design points and trade-offs:
- Ephemeral reserve is small (default 5% of GPU free mem) and elastic up to a policy limit (default 12%). Small reserve keeps failure surface limited; elasticity reduces unnecessary cold-falls.
- Soft-lease tokens make the rebalancer cooperative with the batching layer: batchers can request X tokens; grant is probabilistic based on current pressure to avoid head-of-line blocking. This trades complexity in scheduler for better tail latency under mixed workloads.
- Eviction-cost heuristic prefers evicting low-reuse KV entries first, then compressing large activation tensors (float16->int8 path) if model supports it, and only rejects requests as last resort. Compression paths will be measured in perf vs. quality and gated per-model.
- Continuous loop runs at 200ms tick by default to balance reaction speed vs. jitter. Simulation shows 200ms is a good starting point for our workload mix.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in OOM incidents on dev clusters during 2-week dogfood compared to baseline (<= baseline OOM count).
- 90th/99th token latency under mixed (chat + completion) synthetic workload reduces by >= 8% / >= 6% respectively vs. static-ledger baseline while maintaining equal or better throughput per GPU.
- Token throughput improves by >= 6% on steady-state low-variance workloads.
- Observability: Grafana dashboard available for ephemeral reserve utilization, rebalancer decisions, eviction reasons, and soft-lease grants.

Test plan:
1) Unit tests for allocation arithmetic and soft-lease handshake.
2) Microbenchmarks (memprobe) that run targeted scenarios: long-context KV-heavy chat, short-burst completion, and blended traces replayed from production traces (sanitized).
3) Cluster simulation: run the existing simulator with mixed tenant profiles and compare OOM count, p95/p99 latency, and GPU utilization against the static-ledger baseline (run at least 100 seed combinations).
4) Canary rollout: deploy to a single machine pool, run canary traffic, validate metrics, then expand to 10% of runtime fleet for 48h before full rollout.

Rollout & mitigation strategy:
- Default policy is conservative: ephemeral reserve capped at 8% for first canary.
- If OOMs spike, rebalancer enters safe-mode (reverts to static ledger) automatically and alerts SRE runbook.
- Provide per-customer opt-out flag and model-level guardrails (models that fail compression or have strict accuracy SLAs will not use aggressive eviction/compression).

Implementation milestones:
- Milestone A (2 weeks): ERO core loop, allocation accounting, and soft-lease API.
- Milestone B (2 weeks): Eviction-cost heuristic, basic KV eviction path, instrumentation.
- Milestone C (2 weeks): Compression path integration (model opt-in), simulator runs and dashboard.
- Milestone D (1 week): Canary deploy + monitoring, automated rollback hooks.
